newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Thai foreign minister in Vietnam to boost ties.
newsitem.headline: Thai foreign minister in Vietnam to boost ties.

text.p: The foreign ministers of Vietnam and Thailand agreed on Wednesday to step up economic cooperation between their two countries and resolve long-running differences over maritime territory.

"We have discussed economic cooperation and Thai investment in Vietnam," Vietnamese Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam told reporters after a meeting in Hanoi with his Thai counterpart, Prachuab Chaiyasarn.
Vietnam and Thailand, both members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), have growing economic links.
Thailand is the ninth-biggest investor in Vietnam, having committed more than $1 billion for 72 projects. Two-way trade between the countries was around $620 million in 1996.

However, the two have not always seen eye to eye on potentially oil-rich maritime territory. Scores of fishermen from both Vietnam and Thailand have in the past been arrested for fishing in waters which each country considers its own.
The foreign ministry said last week that all fishermen being detained in both Vietnam and Thailand had now been released.
Prachuab told a news conference later that Thailand was now hoping for the return of 18 fishing boats still being held by Vietnamese local authorities.
He said the two sides would establish a joint group to discuss differences over maritime areas and a special meeting would be held on the issue in Vietnam in May.

"I think step by step will lead to the solution to these differences. I will not say dispute, but differences." Prachuab signed an agreement with Cam on bilateral cooperation in science and technology before meeting Vietnamese Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet and Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi.
His visit, which aimed to lay the groundwork for a visit by Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh on March 30-31, will end in Ho Chi Minh City on Friday.
